features.name: Refund-pacing runway engine (per-week safe-to-spend number)
features.description: Model a lump-sum aid refund across the known academic term into a rolling per-week safe-to-spend figure that self-corrects as actual spend lands. Core wedge (MDRC RCT validates lump-sum-to-shortfall). No competitor prices refunds as a depleting runway.
features.persona: Refund-Runway Rae — 'When I receive a lump-sum refund, I want to know how much I can safely spend per week so the money lasts.'

features.name: Passive bank-transaction ingestion + auto-classification
features.description: Aggregator-linked (Plaid-class) transaction feed with auto-categorization so student never manually categorizes. Feeds actual spend into pacing engine. Effort carries integration/SOC2 multiplier.
features.persona: Refund-Runway Rae / First-Budget Finn — 'I want to know where my money is going without data entry.'

features.name: Ambient one-number surface (low-touch home view + passive nudge)
features.description: Surface the single trustworthy safe-to-spend number with near-zero required interaction, tuned against anxiety-avoidance (43-49% of Gen Z avoid checking balances). Directly answers the load-bearing contradiction: anxious users avoid engagement-heavy dashboards.
features.persona: Refund-Runway Rae / First-Budget Finn (emotional) — 'I want to feel calm confidence money will last without confronting a spreadsheet.'

features.name: Academic-calendar & aid-disbursement term modeling (manual/guided setup)
features.description: Capture term boundaries, refund amount and expected next-disbursement date so runway has a defined horizon. Launch is guided/manual entry before automated SIS sync exists. Prerequisite domain model for pacing engine.
features.persona: Refund-Runway Rae — 'I want the tool to understand my term and refund cadence.'

features.name: Institutional onboarding: SSO + roster-aware deployment
features.description: Financial-aid-office onboarding path with campus SSO and roster-aware provisioning. Primary B2B2C distribution channel, RICE Reach multiplier. Effort loaded by institutional-integration multiplier.
features.persona: Refund-Runway Rae (via institution) + financial-aid office as buyer — 'I want to deploy a retention-supporting tool to my aid-refund students at scale.'

features.name: SOC2 Type II compliance & student-data privacy posture
features.description: SOC2 Type II and privacy controls. Deal prerequisite for institutional contracts and brand trust pillar. Not user-facing but gates the B2B2C channel; large effort, near-zero incremental reach alone but multiplies institutional path.
features.persona: Financial-aid office (buyer) + all student personas (trust) — 'I need proof student data is safe before I deploy or trust this.'

features.name: Predictive shortfall alerts
features.description: Ambiently warn when projected spend will exhaust runway before term-end, with suggested weekly adjustment. Deepens core value (prevention vs tracking) but v2+ per upstream; depends on stable pacing engine and spend history.
features.persona: Refund-Runway Rae — 'I want to be warned before I run short, not after.'

features.name: Subscription detection & cancel-reminder ('save-me-money' hook)
features.description: Detect recurring subscriptions from transaction feed, surface forgotten/unwanted ones (Gen Z wastes ~$276/yr; 55% forget subs). Monetization/WTP hook (Student Plus) and concrete ROI story; adjacent to core runway job, not the wedge itself.
features.persona: Subscription-Stack Sky / First-Budget Finn — 'I want to be reminded what I'm still paying for so I can cancel waste.'

features.name: First-timer budgeting scaffolding / light literacy guidance
features.description: Minimal, non-lecturing guidance explaining the safe-to-spend number and what 'normal' pacing looks like for genuine first-time managers (avg ~2/6 literacy questions). Reduces onboarding drop-off without becoming an engagement-heavy education product.
features.persona: First-Budget Finn — 'I want simple guidance on my money without feeling overwhelmed.'

features.name: Institutional analytics dashboard (anonymized outcome reporting)
features.description: Aggregate, anonymized outcome reporting for aid offices to justify renewal/expansion. v2+ per upstream; drives institutional retention/expansion but not initial student value; depends on deployed institutional base and SOC2.
features.persona: Financial-aid office (buyer) — 'I need evidence of impact to renew and expand the license.'

features.name: Multi-refund / multi-term & irregular-income modeling
features.description: Handle staggered disbursements, work-study/part-time wage income, multi-semester runway. Real for ICP but an extension of core engine; deferred to v2+ to keep P0 minimal.
features.persona: Refund-Runway Rae — 'I want pacing to hold up across staggered aid and irregular paychecks.'

features.name: Aid-disbursement / SIS integration (auto refund-schedule sync)
features.description: Direct sync of refund schedule from institutional/SIS systems for zero-setup pacing at scale. High long-term leverage but high integration effort per institution and low current confidence; v2+.
features.persona: Refund-Runway Rae (via institution) + aid office — 'I want pacing to just work with no setup.'

features.name: Student Plus tier depth (personalization, safety-cushion goals, export)
features.description: Richer personalization, goal-based 'safety cushions', data export as the $1.99/mo monetization layer for secondary Gen Z segment, without compromising free-forever institutional distribution asset. Monetization polish, not core problem-solving.
features.persona: Subscription-Stack Sky / First-Budget Finn (paid consumer) — 'I want deeper control and goals and I'll pay a little for it.'

sources.description: Upstream product-strategy-agent artifact — vision, positioning, core competencies, RICE framework, explicit deferral of expense splitting
Upstream target-audience-agent artifact — five personas, ICP, Pell-proxy sizing
Upstream problem-discovery-agent artifact — problem severity, underserved gaps, MDRC RCT validating lump-sum-to-shortfall
Upstream user-research-agent artifact — JTBD list, assumption checks (confirmed/contradicted/unconfirmed); secondary/desk research only, confidence 0.48 caps overall scores

gaps: All upstream evidence is secondary/desk research (user-research confidence 0.48); no primary interviews. Feature-level Confidence scores directional until validated.
No quantified reach inputs (addressable students per institution, aid-office adoption rate) — Reach scores relative/ordinal, not derived from real funnel.
No engineering effort estimates — Effort scores (bank-integration, SOC2 multiplier) are placeholders; will shift RICE ordering.
Pacing-accuracy tolerance undefined, yet central to P0 engine Impact.
Minimum ambient-UX interaction threshold that avoids anxiety-driven churn unvalidated.
RICE scores use 1-10 impact scale per task instruction, not strategy artifact's 0.25/0.5/1/2/3 scale; absolute scores not directly comparable.
Expense-splitting demand intentionally excluded from P0/P1; true retention lift remains untested.
nextSteps: Deliver scored backlog to mvp-planning-agent to cut P0 set into MVP scope.
Request quantified reach and engineering effort inputs to convert ordinal RICE into decision-grade scores.
Validate P0 priorities with real target students (n>=5 per persona), testing contradicted 'anxious users engage' assumption.
Define pacing-accuracy tolerance target with users before committing engine acceptance criteria.
Keep expense splitting deferred; only reintroduce after dedicated validation experiment.
Escalate: do NOT attach any delivery deadline to these priorities without explicit human approval.
